lots.what_it_is: Framed colour print of two thylacines after John Gould's Mammals of Australia plate (Gowans title: THYLACINE PRINT). Enlarged crop of the lines under the image reads 'H C Richter del et lith' (left), 'THYLACINUS CYNOCEPHALUS.' (centre) and 'Hullmandel & Walton Imp' (right), matching the Gould plate. Almost certainly a later reproduction, not an 1850s to 1860s original lithograph.
lots.score_reason: Thylacine images sell well in Tasmania, but this looks like a decorative reproduction in a modern frame. That kind of piece usually makes tens of dollars, perhaps up to about A$100. I found no price evidence, so the score is a judgement from the photo only. An original plate would be worth thousands, but nothing in the photo points to one.

lots.key_photo_findings: One photo. The paper is bright white and evenly coloured, with no visible toning or foxing. The colour looks crisp and even, like a photomechanical print, not hand colouring. The edges of the sheet are hidden by the mount, so size and margins cannot be checked.

lots.what_it_is: Samick Stratocaster-style electric guitar in a black shaped hard case (Gowans title: ELECTRIC GUITAR IN HARD CASE). 'Samick' script logo read on an enlarged crop of the headstock. Three-tone sunburst body, cream or white pickguard, three single-coil pickups, vintage-style tremolo bridge (no arm visible), rosewood board with dot inlays. Model, series and serial number not visible. Most likely an entry-level Korean or Indonesian Samick Strat copy.
lots.score_reason: Budget Strat copies in a hard case usually sell second-hand for roughly A$80 to 200, but I found no price evidence to support that. I scored it down because the model is unknown and the electrics are untested.
